speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a critical sign that requires immediate investigation. To begin narrowing down the cause, can you tell me exactly how many days old your baby is, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus

The onset of bilious vomiting within six hours of birth in a term infant is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. Given the history of an older brother with pyloric stenosis, could you please rule out any confusion and confirm that the baby is indeed a newborn who has not been fed yet? Additionally, REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound to check for malrotation and REQUEST IMAGES: Upper GI_Series to definitively visualize the position of the duodenum.
